submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on passages whose subject matter is the mind and the brain: the entities and claims of neuroscience and cognitive psychology (neurons, synapses, hippocampus, cortex, dopamine, memory, attention, perception, emotion, language, psychiatric and neurological disorder). Substantially weaker but still above threshold, it also rises on scholarly discourse about the arts and sciences (universities, departments, professors, disciplines, papers and citations), while matched passages about commerce, finance, law, engineering, machines, plants or everyday events - and the same words in a technical sense, such as a computer's memory or a company's working capital - stay below a quarter of peak. Because the receptive field is a whole phrase of roughly 20-40 tokens, the single highest token is usually a function word (of, the, in, and, or) or a sub-word piece inside such a passage rather than a fixed trigger word.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Volunteers who learned sixty unrelated word pairs in the evening and then slept at home recalled more of them the next morning than a matched group kept awake until dawn, an advantage that survived controls for time of testing and for how confident each person felt. A second study found the benefit vanished when the interval was filled with a demanding task, which the authors take to mean that the gain depends on a quiet period rather than on the mere passage of time.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Core cognitive psychology (learning, recall, consolidation) paraphrased without the top examples' vocabulary; the hypothesis says mind-and-brain subject matter fires.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Depression is more than sadness: it is a persistent loss of interest and energy that can last for months. Treatment usually begins with talking therapy, and medication such as an SSRI is added when symptoms are severe or do not lift. Most people need several weeks before noticing a change, and about half will try a second drug before finding one that suits them. Stopping abruptly can bring on dizziness and irritability, so doctors taper the dose.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Psychiatric disorder and its treatment in a popular-health register, a genre unlike the examples; the hypothesis explicitly lists psychiatric disorder as activating.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The Department of English at the university has, since the 1980s, shifted its hiring toward scholars working on postcolonial fiction, and the department's journal now receives more submissions from South Asia than from any other region. Professors in the programme supervise dissertations on translation and on the nineteenth-century novel, and citation patterns in the field show a growing reliance on a handful of theory journals first published in the 1990s.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Scholarly discourse about the arts with the claimed tokens Department, University, journal, professors and citations but no brain content: the hypothesis's weaker second tier, which it says rises above threshold.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
It was a Tuesday in March, and I was late for a piano lesson I had not wanted to take. I had been working too much that winter, and I had promised my sister I would do one thing that had nothing to do with deadlines, so I signed up for eight weeks of beginners' lessons at a church hall two streets from the flat. I remember standing at the crossing, waiting for the light, thinking about a spreadsheet I had left open on the office computer, and then a grey curtain seemed to come down over the right-hand side of the view, as though somebody had slid a lens across it.

I got across the road anyway. I did not fall. What I felt was puzzlement rather than fear, the kind of puzzlement you feel when a word you have used all your life will not come, and I remember trying to say something to a woman with a dog and hearing a sentence come out of me with the middle missing. She asked if I was all right. What I wanted to say was that I was fine, that I was only late, that this sometimes happened when I had not eaten. What came out was shorter and slower and not really arranged.

At the hospital they did the usual things: a cuff on the arm, an ECG, a cannula, questions about when the symptoms had begun and whether I had taken aspirin that morning. My sister arrived and answered for me, which was easier, though I could hear myself trying to help and failing. In the afternoon a porter wheeled me down a long corridor to a scanner, and I lay in the tube listening to the magnets thud and thinking, absurdly, about the piano teacher and whether she would charge me for the missed lesson.

The next morning a young doctor came in with the pictures on a screen and pointed to a bright patch on the left side of my own brain, in the territory that carries the machinery of speech: the part that, when it loses its blood supply, turns a fluent adult into somebody who knows what a word means but cannot fetch it out. He said the clot had almost certainly come from the heart, and that the window for the dissolving drug had closed while I was still standing at the crossing thinking about the spreadsheet. He said that language comes back better than almost anything else, especially in the first months, because the tissue around the damaged patch can take up some of the work, and because the brain is not a machine with fixed parts but something that rearranges itself when it is pressed.

For a year I could not read a menu without losing the thread, and I learned to order by pointing. I went back to the piano in the autumn, badly and slowly, and my teacher, who had heard what happened, never once mentioned the lesson I missed. What stays with me is not the weakness in my hand, which is mostly gone, but the memory of standing at that crossing, entirely myself and entirely unable to say so.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long first-person memoir with the brain-and-language material deep in a passage of over 500 tokens: tests the feature in an unusual position and a genre unlike the examples, which the hypothesis still predicts fires.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Stand in a crowded room and you can follow one conversation while dozens of others blur into a wash of sound, until somebody across the table says your name and the wash resolves again into words. Psychologists call this selective listening, and they have shown that people register almost nothing of the ignored channel beyond its pitch and the sex of the speaker. In one classic demonstration, listeners wearing headphones repeated aloud one of two simultaneous messages, and midway through, the other message switched briefly into German; hardly anyone reported it afterwards.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cognitive psychology of attention and perception in a magazine register, expressed with notice, register, reported rather than the examples' vocabulary; the hypothesis predicts it fires.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The allocator reserves a block of memory on the heap and hands back a pointer; when the last reference goes out of scope the runtime frees it. Because the collector runs concurrently, a thread may observe a stale address for a few microseconds before the write barrier repairs the table. Profiling showed that ninety per cent of the retained bytes came from one cache keyed by request id, and shortening the key shrank the resident set by half.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Memory in its computing sense inside a systems-programming passage, the exact technical usage the hypothesis says stays below a quarter of peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Working capital fell to $2.1 million from $4.8 million as receivables aged past ninety days and two distributors stretched their terms. The controller posted a journal entry reclassifying $600,000 of inventory, and management drew on the revolver to cover the seasonal build while the bank waived the leverage covenant for one quarter. Gross margin held at 31 per cent, but the auditors added a going-concern note to the filing.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Finance passage built on the hypothesis's own example of a technical sense, working capital, plus journal entry; the hypothesis says commerce and finance stay low.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Engineers describe the central controller as the brain of the machine: it reads a hundred sensor channels, plans a path through the warehouse, and tells each joint how much torque to apply. In trials the cell cut cycle time by eighteen per cent.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Engineering text using brain and remembers metaphorically of a machine controller; the hypothesis says machines, and these words in a technical sense, stay low.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: In a transverse section of the young stem, the cortex lies between the epidermis and the vascular cylinder and consists of several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells. Starch grains accumulate in the inner cortical cells, and in older stems the outermost layers develop into collenchyma that stiffens the shoot. The pith, by contrast, is spongy and may break down to form a hollow cavity.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cortical and cells in plant anatomy: the claimed token in a botanical sense, and the hypothesis says passages about plants stay below a quarter of peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: On the way out I remembered I had left the keys upstairs, so I ran back and found them under the newspaper. At the station I noticed a woman in a green coat who looked like someone I used to work with, but I could not think of her name and did not want to stare. On the train I paid attention to nothing at all and watched the fields go past.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Everyday narrative using mental verbs (remembered, noticed, think, paid attention) but making no claim about mind or brain; the hypothesis says everyday events stay low.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We train the network for thirty epochs with Adam and a batch size of sixty-four. Each neuron in the hidden layer computes a weighted sum of its inputs, adds a bias, and passes the result through a rectified linear unit; gradients flow back through the same weights. Validation accuracy plateaued at 87 per cent, and dropout in the final layer reduced overfitting on the smaller classes.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Neuron and network in machine learning, the same words in a technical sense about machines, which the hypothesis says stays below a quarter of peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Consumer perception of the brand improved after the packaging refresh, according to a quarterly tracker of 4,000 shoppers. adversarial_test_results.detail: Perception and recall in a marketing-research sense inside a commerce passage; the hypothesis lists commerce and technical senses as staying low.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The seahorse (Hippocampus) is a small marine fish with a prehensile tail and a tubular snout, found in shallow seagrass beds. Aquarists find the genus difficult to keep, since captive specimens rarely accept frozen food.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hippocampus appears only as the seahorse genus in a descriptive natural-history entry, with no brain referent; the hypothesis is a claim about mind-and-brain subject matter, so it predicts this stays low.
